conclusion.causalChain: Cause: total stablecoin supply fell $5.89B over thirty days and spot BTC and ETH ETFs have mostly redeemed. Intermediate: usable market liquidity falls and spot marginal bids thin, while the 10-year real yield at 2.66% raises the discount rate. Effect: downside pressure on BTC and ETH. Condition: the read holds while stablecoins keep contracting or ETFs fail to turn into sustained inflows; sustained inflows would break the mechanism.
conclusion.change: No new comparable change this round. The latest readings are stablecoin supply -$857M over one day, -$2.088B over seven days and -$5.89B over thirty days; BTC spot ETFs +$110M and ETH spot ETFs -$88.6M on 26 October.
conditions: Total stablecoin supply keeps contracting, or at least does not recover.
Spot BTC and ETH ETFs do not show multi-day net inflows.
The 10-year real yield stays at 2.66% or higher.
Funding stays mildly positive, with no short squeeze from extreme negative funding.
dataGaps: No cross-asset or price data: the immediate transmission from flows to BTC and ETH prices cannot be verified, so short-horizon confidence is lower.
No market consensus: the surprise in published macro data cannot be sized, so only actuals and priors are comparable.
Sentiment items are stale and not comparable: they are not evidence of current risk appetite.
Some macro events are still pending: the policy rate, GDP and PCE are unknown and could change the rate and liquidity mechanism.
Official daily closes can lag several trading days: rate and ETF data carry a delay, so long-horizon reads deserve a discount.
conclusion.evidenceStrength: The bearish side is stronger: stablecoin supply fell $857M, $2.088B and $5.89B over one, seven and thirty days, and ETH ETFs still redeemed $88.6M on 26 October. The bullish side is only $110M of BTC ETF inflows on 26 October plus mildly positive funding, which is not enough to offset the liquidity contraction.
conclusion.macro: The 10-year Treasury yield is 5% and the real yield 2.66%, so the rate side is tight. Published IFO and CBI readings improved but carry no consensus, so the macro signal is negative for crypto risk assets.
conclusion.summary: Downside pressure dominates: stablecoin supply is contracting and spot BTC and ETH ETFs are redeeming, which pulls marginal bids away, while a 2.66% 10-year real yield keeps the discount rate restrictive. Both weigh on BTC and ETH.

directions.rationale: Stablecoin supply fell $857M over one day and ETH ETFs redeemed $88.6M on 26 October, while BTC ETFs only took in $110M on a single day, so short-horizon flows stay negative.
Stablecoin supply fell $2.088B over seven days and $5.89B over thirty days, and spot BTC and ETH ETFs have mostly redeemed, so mid-term liquidity contraction weighs on prices.
A 2.66% 10-year real yield and a 5% 10-year yield, together with a $5.89B thirty-day stablecoin decline, keep long-horizon valuations under pressure.

supportingEvidence.statement: Total stablecoin supply fell $5.89B over thirty days, mid-term evidence of liquidity contraction.
Total stablecoin supply fell $2.088B over seven days, so short- and mid-term liquidity fell together.
Total stablecoin supply fell $857M in the latest day, so the contraction is still running.

transmissionHypotheses.statement: If total stablecoin supply keeps contracting on the 1-, 7- and 30-day horizons (-$857M, -$2.088B and -$5.89B), usable liquidity tightens and marginal bids thin, pressuring BTC and ETH; a reversal to inflows would break the transmission.
If spot BTC and ETH ETFs keep redeeming, issuers must cut spot exposure, which weakens spot demand and pushes BTC and ETH lower; sustained inflows would invalidate the hypothesis.
If the 10-year real yield stays at or above 2.66%, the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset rises and compresses crypto valuations; a clear fall in real yields would ease the pressure.
